card.name: Digits and splits in tables
card.fires_on: Responds to the leading digit "0" of a decimal in dense numeric tables, and to odd split points such as a single letter inside a word or a space before a number. Mostly in tables, reference lists and abbreviation notes.

modes.label: Leading zero of decimals
modes.description: The 0 before a decimal point in crowded tables of values or ranges.

modes.label: Space before a number
modes.description: A space token just before a number in a range or citation.
modes.example: Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences, v.<< >>47, p. 65

modes.label: Odd splits inside words
modes.description: A single letter or short piece in the middle of a term or table header.

card.writes: It promotes odd characters such as ligatures and bullets and suppresses zero-width spaces and non-breaking spaces, so it steers away from invisible spacing characters.
card.plain: It fires on the start of decimals in packed tables and on awkward text breaks, and it pushes away invisible spacing characters.
